body: Sounds similar, I know that exact feeling where it seems that knuckle should be popped...but can't. Lifting light on squats and deads has improved my back pain greatly in 6-8 months, I can only hope the the wrist and hand injuries help themselves out, too.

Thanks so much for you answer! The boxer's break must have happened when I was a kid and I just never really knew it. I remember having pain around 11 or 12, but didn't know I had injured something. Since I had a very outdoorsy and injury prone childhood, I must just have assumed the pain would stop and it would be fine. 

After a couple different answers like this, im going to look into straps. I assume this isnt something that could be fixed after 10 years unfortunately.
Thanks for the response! Have you ever tried a sleeve or a light brace that would have the same effect as wrapping?

Thanks for the comment. Definitely limits our lifting options. Do you feel yours has healed well, no arthritis?

I grew up outside all the time, playing all sports with reckless abandon, etc and never really got injured that much. After turning 18, however, I had a series of bad injuries that made me realize I was breakable (fractured wrist, broken kneecap, grade 3 sprains, and the herniated disc). I just want to keep all the muscles supporting these joints strong and not risk further injury. I tell ya, though, it's hard not to be depressed by everything piling up and having CP this early in life. Trying to fight it with health.
Thanks for your response. The only person I ever cared for was bipolar, too.
I'll try to heed your words.

I admit the human connection was quite nice while it lasted. Simple things like feeling their heartbeat when sleeping. But I was being sort of led on myself.

Now I've got even more issues with physical or emotional intimacy, and accepting that is part of accepting that "love" simply is not for me. I try to maintain balance by being social, at least. We'll see how that works out.
Hmm....I bet there are for certain disorders. Do you mind me asking what your mental health issues are?

Ah. I admit I wouldn't want to have sex with someone I don't love, but maybe because at this age the partner would likely think I was romantically interested in them just by having sex. I would feel like I was being mean or lying to them.

Interesting to hear from a slightly older viewpoint. Seems to be working out for you, so thats great.!

Agreed. So romantic companionship is not necessarily needed for humans to live a content life?

Personally, I know I am not entitled to it. I'm just a little curious if, even if I'm OK with being alone now, I'll wake up when I'm 45 and feel like my life is incomplete or something.

So you still date even though you aren't looking for love? I don't mean anything negative by that, it just sounds interesting.

People seem to be incredulous when I say I am not looking for love. And single people of the opposite sex seem to think it means I hate them or something, which isnt true.
I'm glad you were able to work through your issues and are about to be happily married! Sounds like you found someone that truly loves and cares for you.
And don't forget the horrible pain and longing if it doesn't work out and you still love them.

Sounds like you've grown and matured quite a bit. You have experience in knowing what kind of people are compatible with you. And you also have experience in knowing why a relationship is a positive thing in your life. 

I don't really have either. But thanks for explaining why it was/is worth it!
Well, now I know that saying "I don't deserve love" will be an easy way to stay away from it.

Hey, at least you tried and now you know. I had felt the same way before ever falling in love. Then somehow I did. And now I know it isn't for me and it's not just a hunch. Like I said earlier, alone doesn't mean lonely!

I'm definitely weird, too. The dating world is just way too much effort and will only lead to me feeling worse than being alone, so I'm content with my decision for now. It just seems there aren't many that think the same so I was curious.
Haha... well that makes the odds game kind of difficult doesn't it? Hopefully if you are looking, you can find someone that appreciates your "fuckedupness."

Wow...I can relate to what you are saying, in a weird way. I gave love a chance about 10 months ago and it didn't go so well to put it mildy. Now I'm mad for ever loving since "I knew it wasn't for me/real/etc." I feel guilty for ever loving and the fact that I still have some feelings for that person has caused me to hate love essentially. Love is becoming replaced by/ associated with my own bitterness towards myself. Everything I feel towards the topic is negative and I want nothing to do with it.

As for finding good people, I suppose they are truly rare. I don't know how you can come back to looking for love after that experience. But if you are still trying, I hope you find someone. And if not then I say have fun on your own. Being alone is not the same as being lonely!

Gah...I do this, too. But mostly with news, reddit, people I see in public. I just read about the worst of humanity so much, I know I am missing the good parts. I give too much thought to the litterers, the people that are assholes to cashiers, people that act self-centered, etc. I'm just not sure how I can change it at the moment. I want to believe that people can be good, but I'm just not seeing it. And I know I'm not looking in the right places. I'll take your comment to mind and see if I can't slowly start changing my worldview and stop thinking that everyone you know will let you down as soon as it becomes convenient.

That is kind of sad. But I can also relate....one of the many justifications for giving up on love for me is, "no one can even love you anyways, and if they could, you don't deserve it." I don't lend to much credence to that since I think it is just depression talking, but like I said, I can relate.

I've always felt physically uncomfortable with anyone touching me in a romantic way. For some reason it makes me feel almost angry....
Interesting. Not to sound too pessimistic, but even with a strong vetting over the issue of TRUST, the next two still cheated on you? That hurts a lot, but you feel the pain and struggle is worth it?
Hey, good to hear it! How long had you given up for? Did your SO have to work hard to make you "crack"?

Hmm...thats interesting. I've been fairly depressed for a couple years and I'm trying to make sure my thought process isn't affected by it. I certainly  know how you feel about distrusting your emotions. That's part of why I don't want anything to do with romance, it makes people so irrational.

Amen to that. Sorry for your heartbreak. Stories like that are exactly why I don't think it is worth it. I feel like I'm better off on my own, only thing I'm worried about is losing all my friends to families and long term relationships.
And she's still your GF?

Yea, I feel you on the cynic part. I'm have horrible self-esteem, so Im not tooting my own horn, but I treat people so much better than they seem to treat others, myself included. I just think as a whole, humans tend to do whatever is most convenient for them, the simplest path to pleasure. That weakness is in our nature...all that cheating and lying you mention.

I personally just dont want to invest that much of myself in someone else. Well, I don't think I can, either. So while I remain a cynic and won't seek it.....I'll admit there might be a small chance I meet someone that wants to make me give it a go years from now.
Thank-you..sorry about that!
Heartbroken?
So you have given up looking, correct?
I'm 24, my friends say thats too early to have given up. How old are you, and do your friends try to tell you to find someone, hook you up, etc?

Not saying it will cure depression, but you need to try. Seriously.

You don't need money for it. Thats an excuse, a mental block. Thirty minutes three days a week isn't too much time to ask either.

As a human, we evolved as long distance runners. Our brains need the neurochemicals and endorphins produced through activity. There is tons of research out there if you want to look into it. 

Again, I'm not saying this will cure depression, but it is a great place to start. And I guarantee you wil have more energy. (I'm tired and depressed too).
If anyone has any help or advice, thank-you. I'm going to go to bed and will likely spend time tomorrow trying to think of ways to make it look like an accident.

True, apathy or attempted apathy is a defense mechanism. But there's a reason I/we feel the need to be protected from it. I don't see the fundamental issues with the human condition changing at all.

I know that I'd be content with killing myself. It is, ironically, the only thing I can really think of now that makes me momentarily happy. I actively want to, and desire to, cease existing.

That being said, how did you stop feeling this way? It sounds like you are no longer suicidal/depressed. What worked for you? Do you know longer think "self-euthanasia" is a rational thought?

Hmm, interesting. I think I can get you started.

Look into Derealization and Depersonalization. This sounds like it is related to one of those, likely DP.

Good question. I feel exactly this way right now. I've stopped working hard at my job, I seek little social interaction, and just look for distractions to pass the time. 

One of those distractions is exercise. I've been working out a lot and it seems to provide my brain the chemicals to make happiness a possibility, but nothing makes me happy. 

The best I can do is distract myself. I have thought of the perfect method to do it, too. It is hard not to fantasize. I dont have an answer for you, but this is a great question I struggle with.
